kf: Common inflammatory dermatitis of the hands: **irritant**, **allergic**, **atopic** and **vesicular (pompholyx)** patterns, often mixed.
Chronic hand eczema affects about **1 in 10** adults; frequent cause of time off work.
High-risk jobs: healthcare, cleaning, catering, hairdressing, construction, metalwork (wet work and chemicals).
Management: avoid irritants, **gloves**, frequent emollients, soap substitute, **potent topical steroid** short courses; patch test if allergy possible.
Refer if severe, not responding, occupational or diagnostic doubt (tinea, psoriasis).

sub: Hand dermatitis accounts for 20–35% of all dermatitis; chronic hand eczema affects 10–15% of adults.
More common in **young adult women** and people with **atopic eczema**.
Wet work (over 2 hours a day or frequent handwashing) is the main risk factor; leading cause of occupational skin disease.

aet: **Irritants**: water, soaps, detergents, alcohol rubs, solvents, cutting oils, dusts, cold and friction.
**Allergens**: rubber accelerators (gloves), preservatives, fragrances, chromate, nickel, hair dyes, acrylates (nails), plants.
**Endogenous**: atopy, filaggrin mutations, pompholyx (often triggered by heat, sweating, stress, nickel).
myths: **"Alcohol gel is worse than soap"**: alcohol rubs are usually less irritant than repeated soap and water.
**"Gloves all day protect the skin"**: long occlusion causes sweat irritation; use cotton liners.
patho_lead: Hand eczema is driven by **barrier damage** with or without an **allergic** (type IV) response.

mech.t: Repeated wet work and detergents strip lipids from the stratum corneum, increasing water loss and irritation.
mech.cap: Patterns of hand eczema: irritant (backs and finger webs), allergic (glove or contact pattern), atopic and pompholyx (vesicles on palms and sides of fingers).

mech.t: Damaged keratinocytes release cytokines; in allergic cases, sensitised T cells respond to specific allergens.
In pompholyx, intense spongiosis in thick palmar skin forms deep itchy **vesicles** that do not easily rupture.
mech.cap: Pompholyx: deep, tapioca-like vesicles held within thick palmar epidermis.

mech.t: Ongoing exposure causes hyperkeratosis, painful **fissures** and lichenification.

histo: Spongiotic dermatitis; pompholyx shows intraepidermal vesicles in acral skin; chronic disease shows acanthosis and hyperkeratosis.
Scrapings exclude tinea; patch testing identifies allergens.

sub: Involve occupational health early; alcohol rubs plus emollients reduce irritation.

comp: Painful fissures, secondary infection (*S. aureus*), eczema herpeticum.
Loss of work and income; long-term disability.
prog: Often chronic and relapsing; only about half are clear years later, especially with atopy, allergy or continued exposure.
Early diagnosis, glove use and job adaptation improve outlook.
